title: Go: Interfaces
description: Define and implement interfaces, use interfaces as parameters, type assertions, and the empty interface.

steps.title: Define an Interface
steps.description: Define a `Speaker` interface with a `Speak() string` method. Create a `Dog` struct that implements it and call `Speak()`.
hints: `type Dog struct{}` with `func (d Dog) Speak() string { return "Woof!" }`

verification.failureMessage: Define Speaker interface, implement it on Dog, print 'Woof!'.

steps.title: Implicit Implementation
steps.description: Create a `Cat` struct that also implements `Speaker` with `"Meow!"`. There is no explicit `implements` keyword. Print both.
hints: Go uses structural typing — no `implements` keyword.
Assign both to a `Speaker` variable: `var s Speaker`.

verification.failureMessage: Make Dog and Cat both implement Speaker implicitly, print both.

steps.title: Interface as Parameter
steps.description: Write a function `printSpeak(s Speaker)` that calls `s.Speak()` and prints the result. Pass a Dog and a Cat to it.
hints: Any type that implements Speaker can be passed.

verification.failureMessage: Write printSpeak that accepts Speaker and call it with Dog and Cat.

steps.title: Type Assertion
steps.description: Declare `var i interface{} = "hello"`. Use a type assertion to extract the string value and print it.
hints: `s := i.(string)` asserts that i holds a string.
Without `ok` check, it panics if wrong type.

verification.failureMessage: Assert and print the string value 'hello' from an interface{}.

steps.title: Empty Interface
steps.description: Write a function `describe(i interface{})` that prints the value and its type using `%T`. Call it with an int, string, and bool.
hints: `func describe(i interface{}) { fmt.Printf("Value: %v, Type: %T\n", i, i) }`

verification.test: output.includes('42') && output.includes('Go') && output.includes('true') && output.includes('int') && output.includes('string') && output.includes('bool')
verification.failureMessage: Write describe(i interface{}) printing value and type for int, string, bool.
